Done. Summary of what I found and did: ## Diagnosis `Location: ///i8n.example2.com/302` is a network-path reference with an extra leading slash. `urlsplit('///i8n.example2.com/302')` parses it as an **empty netloc** with path `/i8n.example2.com/302`, so `urljoin(request.url, location)` resolved it against the original host: ``` 'http://www.example.com/302' + Location '///i8n.example2.com/302' -> 'http://www.example.com/i8n.example2.com/302' (wrong host) ``` Browsers tolerate the extra slash and treat it as `//i8n.example2.com/302` (scheme-relative), so Scrapy should too. ## Fix In `scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/redirect.py`, when the raw `Location` header value starts with `//`, rebuild it as `<request-scheme>://<host/path>` (stripping all leading slashes) before `urljoin`:

```python location = safe_url_string(response.headers['location']) if response.headers['location'].startswith(b'//'): request_scheme = urlparse(request.url).scheme location = request_scheme + '://' + location.lstrip('/') redirected_url = urljoin(request.url, location) ``` This matches upstream Scrapy's fix. `//` still yields the request scheme, `///+` now collapses to the correct host, and single-slash/absolute/relative `Location` values are untouched. ## Test results - `test_redirect_302_relative`: **was failing** (`'http://www.example.com/i8n.example2.com/302' != 'http://i8n.example2.com/302'`), now passes. - Full `tests.test_downloadermiddleware_redirect` suite: **24 tests, all pass** — including `test_latin1_location`, `test_utf8_location`, `test_redirect_302`, `test_redirect_302_head`, `test_redirect_3xx_permanent`, and the meta-refresh tests. ## Environment note This sandbox had n…
